architecture.text: The field is heavily optimizing long-context and agentic systems, tackling the Proximity Trap and Model Context Protocol vulnerabilities while advancing hyperbolic geometry and hybrid sparse attention to improve memory, efficiency, and 3D-consistent world generation.

new-models.text: Recent advancements focus heavily on domain-specific vision-language models and native multimodal integration, with standout releases like Xiaomi MiMo-V2.6-Pro, MintAct, and OmniVChat. Systems are increasingly prioritizing physical world understanding, complex medical prediction, and advanced agentic reasoning over raw scaling.

inference-methods.text: Inference optimization currently focuses on scaling test-time compute, compressing models through specialized quantization and cross-layer factorization, and managing massive context windows via efficient KV selection and state management.

inference-engines.text: The LLM serving landscape is rapidly evolving to support complex multi-turn agents and video workloads through hardware-aware memory tiering, vLLM prefix caching, and dynamic sparse attention. Simultaneously, infrastructure is shifting toward disaggregated resource allocation and topological cluster scheduling.

silicon.text: AI hardware engineering focuses intensely on maximizing TPU and GPU cluster efficiency, scaling interconnects, and optimizing memory offloading. Practitioners are tackling bottlenecks through low-cost FPGA implementations, advanced optical technologies, and software-level power surge mitigation.

training.text: RLHF and reward hacking dominate current training paradigms, with new frameworks tackling token-level credit assignment, instance-aware rubric rewards, and multi-vector reward hacking across weights and prompts. Concurrently, theoretical work is formalizing neural scaling laws and diffusion model overfitting.
